gen-zen-dots-gf-special-gothic: Techy but friendly, with space around every letter. Zen Dots shows off its wide, generous shapes in big display sizes, while Special Gothic keeps text feeling approachable, with rounded letters that stay open on a plain sans body.
gen-zen-dots-gf-spinnaker: Zen Dots gives every letter a generous patch of breathing space, even at heavy weights. Then Spinnaker follows with a modern sans-serif body whose apertures keep the counters connected to the outside, so the two feel linked.
gen-zen-dots-gf-stick: Stick draws its sans-serif lines like tubing, constant in weight. Zen Dots above it is the one with low horizontals and a display swagger, and the two make a sturdy, friendly tech pairing.
gen-zen-dots-gf-suse: Generous room around every letter is what defines Zen Dots. It carries the display work with a techy, friendly flair, while SUSE, a sans-serif with rope-like curves and open bowls, handles the approachable reading.
gen-zen-dots-gf-suse-mono: SUSE Mono reads professional yet approachable, with open curves and extra space on both sides of every letter. Zen Dots then adds a techy, friendly headline voice, and its roomy shapes echo that spacing nicely.
gen-zen-dots-gf-tajawal: Zen Dots keeps its openings generous at every weight, which gives it a techy, friendly face. Tajawal, a sans-serif with a c like a broad open hook, is the pair's strongest quality: a clean, neutral partner that never competes.
gen-zen-dots-gf-tasa-explorer: Friendly and techy, Zen Dots is the one built to stand out, with lots of room around each letter shape. TASA Explorer is the quiet worker, a plain sans whose curve ends stop like brush strokes lifted early.
gen-zen-dots-gf-tasa-orbiter: Clean and techy, Zen Dots opens up wide. Its display letters are made to catch attention, while TASA Orbiter, a sans-serif with unclogged small counters, is made to keep text crisp and professional.
gen-zen-dots-gf-teachers: Teachers looks like thin steel rod bent into letters, with ink strokes that taper out before touching. But Zen Dots is the one made for display, with generous openings, while the sans-serif body does the modern, pipe-cleaner-light text work.
gen-zen-dots-gf-telex: Zen Dots leaves lots of room around every letter, and its openings stay generous at every weight. So Telex, a clean sans with curvy letters that feel unclamped, slips in underneath as a natural, neutral companion.
